\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വ്യക്തമായ} (vyaktamāya)}{വ്യക്തമായ (vyaktamāya)}]{\ml{വ്യക്തമായ} (vyaktamāya) — evident; clear}

\label{lesson:ML-C446-vyaktamaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for serious, then the Malayalam for complex.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വ്യക്തമായ}}
\textbf{\ml{വ്യക്തമായ}} — \emph{vyaktamāya} — \textquotedblleft{}evident; clear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവൻ} \ml{വ്യക്തമായ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{ഉത്തരം} \ml{നൽകി}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avan vyaktamāya oru uttaraṁ nalki.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He gave a clear answer.
\end{quote}

The adverb is \ml{വ്യക്തമായി}, clearly.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വ്യക്തമായ}} (\emph{vyaktamāya}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{vyakta}, \textquotedblleft{}adorned; manifest, evident\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 12156; Monier-Williams), with the adjective ending -\ml{ആയ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vyaktamāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vyaktamāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avan vyaktamāya oru uttaraṁ nalki.} — He gave a clear answer.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for serious, then the Malayalam for complex, then say \emph{vyaktamāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വ്യക്തമായ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Evident; clear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{പൊതുവായ} (potuvāya)}{പൊതുവായ (potuvāya)}]{\ml{പൊതുവായ} (potuvāya) — common; shared}

\label{lesson:ML-C446-potuvaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for complex, then the Malayalam for evident.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{പൊതുവായ}}
\textbf{\ml{പൊതുവായ}} — \emph{potuvāya} — \textquotedblleft{}common; shared\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{രണ്ട്} \ml{ഭാഷകൾക്കും} \ml{പൊതുവായ} \ml{പല} \ml{വാക്കുകളും} \ml{ഉണ്ട്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raṇṭŭ bhāṣakaḷkkuṁ potuvāya pala vākkukaḷuṁ uṇṭŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The two languages have many words in common.
\end{quote}

Common to two things: -\ml{ക്കും} \ml{പൊതുവായ}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{പൊതുവായ}} (\emph{potuvāya}) is native Dravidian: \ml{പൊതു}, \textquotedblleft{}common, general\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4507), with the adjective ending -\ml{ആയ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{potuvāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{potuvāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{raṇṭŭ bhāṣakaḷkkuṁ potuvāya pala vākkukaḷuṁ uṇṭŭ.} — The two languages have many words in common.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for complex, then the Malayalam for evident, then say \emph{potuvāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{പൊതുവായ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Common; shared\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{ഫലപ്രദമായ} (phalapradamāya)}{ഫലപ്രദമായ (phalapradamāya)}]{\ml{ഫലപ്രദമായ} (phalapradamāya) — effective}

\label{lesson:ML-C446-phalapradamaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for evident, then the Malayalam for common.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{ഫലപ്രദമായ}}
\textbf{\ml{ഫലപ്രദമായ}} — \emph{phalapradamāya} — \textquotedblleft{}effective\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{മരുന്ന്} \ml{വളരെ} \ml{ഫലപ്രദമായിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā marunnŭ vaḷare phalapradamāyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That medicine was very effective.
\end{quote}

\ml{ഫലം}, a result, and -\ml{പ്രദ}, giving: giving results.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{ഫലപ്രദമായ}} (\emph{phalapradamāya}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{phala}, \textquotedblleft{}fruit, result\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9051), and \emph{prada}, \textquotedblleft{}giving, yielding\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the adjective ending -\ml{ആയ}: yielding fruit.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phalapradamāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phalapradamāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā marunnŭ vaḷare phalapradamāyirunnu.} — That medicine was very effective.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for evident, then the Malayalam for common, then say \emph{phalapradamāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{ഫലപ്രദമായ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Effective\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{യുക്തിസഹമായ} (yuktisahamāya)}{യുക്തിസഹമായ (yuktisahamāya)}]{\ml{യുക്തിസഹമായ} (yuktisahamāya) — logical; reasonable}

\label{lesson:ML-C446-yuktisahamaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for common, then the Malayalam for effective.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{യുക്തിസഹമായ}}
\textbf{\ml{യുക്തിസഹമായ}} — \emph{yuktisahamāya} — \textquotedblleft{}logical; reasonable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{അവളുടെ} \ml{വാദം} \ml{യുക്തിസഹമായിരുന്നു}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{avaḷuṭe vādaṁ yuktisahamāyirunnu.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Her argument was logical.
\end{quote}

\ml{യുക്തി}, logic, with -\ml{സഹ}, with: in keeping with logic.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{യുക്തിസഹമായ}} (\emph{yuktisahamāya}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{yukti}, \textquotedblleft{}reasoning\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10480), and \emph{saha}, \textquotedblleft{}together with\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13297), with the adjective ending -\ml{ആയ}: going with reason.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yuktisahamāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yuktisahamāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avaḷuṭe vādaṁ yuktisahamāyirunnu.} — Her argument was logical.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for common, then the Malayalam for effective, then say \emph{yuktisahamāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{യുക്തിസഹമായ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Logical; reasonable\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ} (viśvasanīyamāya)}{വിശ്വസനീയമായ (viśvasanīyamāya)}]{\ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ} (viśvasanīyamāya) — reliable; credible}

\label{lesson:ML-C446-visvasaniyamaya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Malayalam for effective, then the Malayalam for logical.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ}}
\textbf{\ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ}} — \emph{viśvasanīyamāya} — \textquotedblleft{}reliable; credible\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ml{ആ} \ml{വാർത്ത} \ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ} \ml{ഒരു} \ml{ഉറവിടത്തിൽ} \ml{നിന്നാണ്}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā vārtta viśvasanīyamāya oru uṟaviṭattil ninnāṇŭ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
That news is from a reliable source.
\end{quote}

The -\ml{നീയ} ending means fit to be: \ml{വിശ്വസനീയ}, fit to be trusted.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ}} (\emph{viśvasanīyamāya}) is built from Sanskrit \emph{viśvasanīya}, \textquotedblleft{}to be trusted, reliable, credible\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with the adjective ending -\ml{ആയ}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśvasanīyamāya}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśvasanīyamāya}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā vārtta viśvasanīyamāya oru uṟaviṭattil ninnāṇŭ.} — That news is from a reliable source.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Malayalam for effective, then the Malayalam for logical, then say \emph{viśvasanīyamāya} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ml{വിശ്വസനീയമായ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Reliable; credible\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
